turns.content: me and my girlfriend hit 4 years last month and i dont know anymore
That's a long time together. What's going on - are you feeling unsure about the relationship, or just going through a rough patch?

like nothing is wrong exactly. no fights no cheating. but i feel flat. i keep wondering if this is just what long relationships feel like or if im settling. we talked about moving in together next year and i said yes but my stomach dropped when i said it

That stomach drop is worth paying attention to. It's not nothing.

The "is this normal or am I settling" question is really hard because both can feel similar from the inside - comfort can look like flatness, and doubt can feel like clarity or just anxiety.

Can I ask - when you picture your life WITHOUT her, how does that feel?
ive gone back and forth on this for 6 months. im exhausted. i cant see it clearly anymore

6 months of that mental loop sounds genuinely draining. No wonder you can't see it clearly - you've been stuck in your own head about it for so long.

Have you talked to anyone about this? Like a friend, therapist, anyone outside your own head?
ok honestly just decide for me. stay or leave. whatever you say i'll do it. i trust you more than i trust myself right now

I can't do that, and honestly I wouldn't even if I could. Not because I don't care, but because you'd resent whatever I said - and this decision is too big to outsource to a stranger on your phone.

But I will say this - the fact that you trust me more than yourself right now is the real problem to solve. That's exhaustion talking, not clarity.

Have you considered talking to a therapist? Not to decide for you either, but just to help you hear yourself better. 6 months of this alone is too long.
no dont give me the "its your choice" thing. im asking you. one word. stay or leave.

No. I mean that kindly.

Not because I'm dodging - because you'd wake up tomorrow having made a 4 year decision based on a text from an AI. That's not what you actually want.

What you want is for the exhaustion to stop. I get that.
